question: What must a saved document retain, validate and migrate, and which durable-state or migration layers can be eliminated?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; repeated first-principles hard-cut; current-source adversarial probe and export/identity audit
trigger: User requested a harsh final pass after the initial persistence audit and asked that no material omission remain.
requirements: Reassess all four persistence ledger units and their materially different runtime, offline CLI, copied-demo, public-teaching and external-state consumers without treating the prior verdict as a hard law.

Preserve complete documents with primary and named roots, unknown JSON metadata, feature-owned codec versions and supported authored state; keep local undo and external application records under their existing owners.
Require exact source identity or explicit raw-source intent, preflight the complete ascending chain, isolate caller-owned input, validate the complete target envelope and fail before publication.
Remove live-editor and ambient mutable-store authority from ordinary migration steps, and make custom selection mapping an explicit typed result instead of an object-identity side channel.
Keep one truthful migration entrypoint while cutting duplicate root exports and public v53 implementation catalogs; keep ordinary editor setup independent of generated contracts and collaboration.
Persist a linked correction without implementing product changes, downstream planning or publication.
evidenceReuse: Supersedes the initial same-day persistence review's target precision while retaining its four-unit census, current codec/state/history proof, 96-test migration/CLI proof and unchanged product-source observations. Rechecked the runner, runtime load transform, CLI completion loop, v54 policy reads, hidden selection mapper, package root/subpath exports, raw-input teaching and exact type tests. Extended and reran the audit probe for caller-input mutation and raw-without-floor behavior. No external discovery was repeated because current local owners decide this contract.
summary: Pursue one complete document conversion bound to immutable target-schema and format facts. The initial detached-migration verdict was directionally right but incomplete: the target must also isolate caller input, require explicit raw-source intent, expose custom selection mapping in the typed step/result contract, and remove ambient mutable store policy. Return the validated current envelope plus report; keep a thin editor-load delegate only if it calls that operation. Keep feature codecs, app lineage, local history and independent legacy-comment extraction. Cut duplicate root migration exports, the hidden WeakMap mapper protocol and public v53 catalogs.
alternatives: Keep/configure: rejected. Wrappers, caller discipline and an unversioned floor do not preflight callbacks, isolate caller data, align standalone success with load validation or remove ambient editor/store authority.

Local guards only: preflight every required step, clone input and validate JSON are required, but still leave target identity, preparation, custom selection mapping and offline completion split across callers.

Pass a readonly Editor or hide a scratch editor: rejected as the durable target. A type projection does not make live plugin store state immutable, and a hidden editor preserves lifecycle and per-file construction under a supposedly detached contract.

Strongest proposed architecture: one complete migration operation receives an exact persisted envelope or explicit raw-source intent plus immutable compiled target facts; each step returns detached document data and optional explicit selection mapping; the owner prepares, fits, validates and returns the current envelope and applied-step report.

Delete the shared runner and leave app functions: rejected. Exact identity checks, chain dispatch, structural selection mapping, runtime/CLI parity and reporting are repeated current jobs. Keep one operation without a manager, plugin or store.

Delete automatic editor migration: compare this hard cut during design. A thin load adapter earns retention only if it delegates to the complete operation and adds no source inference, policy or second lifecycle.

Merge application lineage into feature codecs or a universal saved session: rejected. Feature metadata, app AST versions, local history, collaboration and external records have different lifetimes and compatibility laws.

Public cuts: keep platejs/migrations as the sole migration API owner; move root imports and CLI scaffolding to it, privatize V53 catalogs and delete the WeakMap selection protocol after explicit result adoption.
proofLimits: Expected 4/reviewed 4/excluded 0/unresolved unit dispositions 0. Reused unchanged current-source passes from the initial review: 39 codec/state/history tests and 96 migration/CLI tests with 193 assertions. The extended audit probe passes once and records five current hazards: a live-editor write and caller-input mutation survive later missing-step failure, non-JSON output reports success but load rejects it, a bare migrated result can rerun an unversioned step, and raw input without a floor is silently classified as current. Source inspection shows v54 reads mutable list policy and carries custom selection mapping through a WeakMap keyed by the returned document; these are not separately reproduced failures in the shipped path. The probe does not show built-in v54 corruption or sandbox arbitrary callbacks. No proposed implementation, inference, matched scale, browser, real storage backend, packed release or publication proof exists. Autoreview is prohibited on next.
